end.summary:
Veer named polygons by their number of straight sides, including shapes in different forms.
Veer recognised triangles and polygons when they were rotated or varied in appearance.
Veer described triangles using equal sides and angle types, including equilateral, isosceles, and right-angled triangles.
They first hesitated on why rotation does not change a triangle, then gave the straight-side explanation later; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised naming polygons, recognising them in different positions, and describing triangles by sides and angles. Veer used the number of straight sides and corners as the method, and later corrected the hesitation about rotated triangles by noting that the sides stay straight and unchanged. At home, show a few rotated or unusual shapes and ask Veer to name them and explain which features stay the same.
